subject: Redwood trial - procurement & billing next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@acme.com>, Emma Li <emma.li@acme.com>
Cc: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-03-28T09:32:00-07:00
Subject: Redwood trial - procurement & billing next steps

Hi Alex / Emma 

Thanks again for the time this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned while your teams run the pilot: 

What we covered:
- Trial scope: 30-day evaluation with the Redwood inference runtime (chat + embeddings) connected to your staging environment.
- Success signals: integration stability, <50ms p95 for token generation on test workloads, and reaching ~50k tokens/day in production-simulated runs.
- Procurement: you mentioned procurement and legal would need standard paperwork and an approved pricing model to move to a paid contract.

Action items / asks for Acme:
1) Procurement path: do you expect to pay by PO or company card for the initial committed capacity? Any $ threshold where card is allowed?
2) Marketplace interest: would Acme prefer an AWS Marketplace purchase (consolidated billing) or direct Redwood invoicing?
3) Success criteria: please confirm the core metric(s) you want us to monitor to signal readiness to bill.
4) Target billing start date: any preferred start date if trial goes well?

I attached the latest SOW draft and our standard pricing sheet for reference  these are the starting point and can be adjusted based on procurement feedback.

Attachments: SOW-acme-v1.pdf, redwood-pricing-2027.xlsx

If helpful I can loop in our security lead (Nikhil) to fast-follow on SOC2 evidence and any technical/controls questions.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0198

From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Emma Li <emma.li@acme.com>, Procurement <procurement@acme.com>
Date: 2027-03-28T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood trial - procurement & billing next steps

Hi Marissa 

Great call  thanks for the summary. A few clarifications from procurement/legal side: 

- Payment method: For pilots > $10k we typically require a PO. Cards are allowed for small purchases under $10k only.
- Procurement system: we use ServiceNow for PO submissions and approvals; procurement@acme.com is the contact.
- Timeline: internal approvals normally take 24 weeks once we have the SOW and pricing confirmed.
- Security: we will need SOC2 Type II evidence and a short summary of data handling and retention.

I'm attaching our PO template for your procurement team to review.

We are interested in Marketplace (AWS) if it simplifies finance, but we have to confirm discounts and invoicing cadence.

Thanks 
Alex Turner
Head of Platform Integrations | Acme Corp
alex.turner@acme.com | (650) 555-0112

Attachments: Acme-PO-template.docx

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@acme.com>, Emma Li <emma.li@acme.com>
Cc: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Procurement <procurement@acme.com>
Date: 2027-03-28T13:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood trial - procurement & billing next steps

Alex  perfect, thanks for the clarity. A few notes from our side and proposed mutual action plan: 

1) PO path / timeline
- We can accept a PO via ServiceNow. Our finance team will review Acme's PO template; attaching a short SOW and our standard terms for alignment.

2) Marketplace option
- We support AWS Marketplace (private offers)  Nikhil, can you and I pull together a one-pager comparing direct invoicing vs Marketplace (fees, billing cadence, discounts)? I'll include that in the package.

3) Security / SOC2
- Nikhil  Im looping you in to provide SOC2 summary and any technical artifacts Acme needs. We have a SOC2 summary and SOC2 reports available under NDA.

4) Trial-to-paid success criteria and billing start
- From our earlier convo I heard: integration stable + 50k tokens/day sustained for 3 days. Can you confirm?
- Suggested target billing start (if success criteria met): 2027-04-25  would that align with your approval timing?

5) Canary PO ask
- If it helps speed things up, would Acme consider issuing a smaller initial PO that covers the first month of committed capacity (we can then follow with the main PO/contract)?

Next steps:
- Ill share a short comparison doc (direct vs marketplace) and a redwood SOC2 summary by EOD today.
- Marissa / Nikhil to review Acme PO template and respond to procurement@acme.com with any questions.

Attachments: Redwood-SOC2-summary.pdf, AWS-Marketplace-overview.pdf, SOW-acme-v1.pdf

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai

From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@acme.com>
Date: 2027-03-29T09:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood trial - procurement & billing next steps

Marissa / team 

Thanks  confirmation below: 
- Success criteria: integration stable, no critical security findings from our pen test / controls review, and hitting ~50k tokens/day for 3 consecutive days during the pilot.
- Payment path: PO (ServiceNow)  Procurement confirms they can process a canary PO for initial capacity and then follow with the full PO once security and integration checks are green.
- Marketplace: we prefer direct invoicing unless the Marketplace offer is materially simpler for discounts / approvals. We should have a decision on Marketplace by the end of the week.
- Target billing start: aiming for 2027-04-25 as a go-live/billing start if the pilot meets the success criteria.

I'll ask procurement to start the PO workflow as soon as you send an updated SOW + pricing. Also, procurement has asked that any enterprise SLA be routed through DocuSign ll send the envelope link once legal has reviewed.

Thanks 
Alex

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-03-29T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: Acme PO path & SOC2 follow-up (for your awareness)

Rishi / Nikhil  quick internal note summarizing where Acme landed: 
- Procurement will require PO for >$10k; they can do a canary PO to start.
- Target billing start (if pilot passes) 2027-04-25.
- Action: Nikhil to get SOC2 summary + any control artifacts to procurement@acme.com and to review Acme-PO-template.docx.
- Ill prepare an updated SOW that references the canary PO approach and include optional Marketplace info for Acme to decide.

Let me know if I should push for any commercial concessions or a short-term credit if approvals run long.

Thanks,
Marissa
